task: Measure blaze against makepad's Relax head to head (D21) and see which rows blaze wins
do: On the Mac, with an installed blaze (the thin `blaze` beside its `blaze-engine`) and nothing else building: `python3 -I harness/v2/versus.py '{"blaze": "<inst>/blaze", "relax": "/tmp/relax-src/relax/target/release/relax", "root": "/private/tmp/versus-<tree>", "tree": "<the blaze checkout>"}'` with a new root per tree (it refuses a non-empty one unless "reuse": true, and anything under ~/.cache/blaze or ~/.blaze). Add `extra` rows for reth and tempo checkouts. Read the table, keep `<root>/versus.json` with the tree's commit; exit 0 means every row won at `factor` (3.0), 1 a lost row, 2 a failed run (named with its output). A full run on the fixtures (hello, six, bstd-hello) takes more than 20 minutes: the idle 45 s and 60 s-idle rows wait 3 times each, per tool and project.
why: Relax's numbers move with the machine and the hour; D21 asks for both tools on one machine, every run checked (a Relax run from the wrong directory exits 1 in 10 ms and looks fast: memstrat-h3).
